title: Revelation: A New Translation with Introduction and Commentary (Anchor Yale Bible 38A)
author: Craig R. Koester
summary: Major critical commentary attentive to social, economic and religious setting and to the book's history of interpretation and influence.

title: The Book of Revelation (NICNT, revised)
author: Robert H. Mounce
summary: Evangelical commentary; late date, apostolic authorship held as probable, a blend of preterist setting and future consummation.

title: Revelation 1–7: An Exegetical Commentary
author: Robert L. Thomas
summary: Detailed dispensational futurist commentary; defends apostolic authorship, a late date and a pretribulational reading of Revelation 3:10.

title: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Revelation of St. John (ICC, 2 vols.)
author: R. H. Charles
summary: Older critical commentary strong on Jewish apocalyptic parallels and Revelation's Semitic Greek; attributes the book to a John other than the apostle.
note: Public-domain work; no URL checked during research.

title: Imperial Cults and the Apocalypse of John: Reading Revelation in the Ruins
author: Steven J. Friesen
summary: Archaeological and textual study of the imperial cults of Roman Asia (Pergamum, Smyrna, Ephesus) and how they illuminate John's critique of empire.

title: The Old Testament Pseudepigrapha (2 vols.)
author: James H. Charlesworth (ed.)
summary: Standard English edition of Second Temple Jewish texts such as 1 Enoch, 4 Ezra, 2 Baruch, Jubilees, the Psalms of Solomon and the Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs, cited here for the Jewish background of Revelation's imagery.
note: Standard reference work; not checked online during research.

title: Revelation, in Commentary on the New Testament Use of the Old Testament (ed. Beale and Carson)
author: G. K. Beale and Sean M. McDonough
summary: Verse-by-verse survey of Revelation's allusions to Daniel, Ezekiel, Isaiah, Zechariah, Exodus and the Psalms, with notes on Jewish interpretive tradition.
